title: A quantitative spectral library of human aqueous humor was analyzed using TimsTOFTM Pro Bruker for primary open angle glaucoma (POAG).
projectDescription: Globally, irreversible vision loss is mainly attributed to glaucoma, a complex eye condition. Given that the progression of glaucoma is challenging to detect and track, and reliable predictive markers are lacking, there is an urgent need for biomarkers. In this context, the aqueous humor, which is part of the anterior segment of the eye, assumes a critical role. The aim of this study is to develop a comprehensive database for glaucoma research by analyzing primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) human aqueous humor samples (n=66). We employ advanced label-free quantitative proteomics to investigate the proteome associated with glaucoma in human aqueous humor. Our dataset, generated using the TimsTOF™ Pro Bruker mass spectrometer and DIA-NN bioinformatics for library-independent quantification of data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, offers researchers access to the most extensive catalog of human aqueous humor proteins reported to date. This resource is expected to deepen our understanding of the proteomic profiles in human glaucoma aqueous humor and also support investigations into proteomes related to other ocular conditions.
sampleProcessingProtocol:
A protein sample (50 μg) of each sample was reduced with 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) for 30 minutes at 37°C. Following reduction, the sample was cooled to room temperature and subsequently alkylated in the dark for 45 minutes at room temperature using 55 mM iodoacetamide (IAA). Ammonium bicarbonate (50 mM) was added to each sample to adjust the volume to 100 μl and mixed thoroughly. Subsequently, the solution was passed through a 10 KDa ultrafiltration tube and centrifuged at 20°C with a speed of 12,000g for 20 minutes. The trapped proteins were then digested with trypsin at a ratio of 40:1 (protein: enzyme) overnight at 37°C. The digested peptides were eluted with 100 μl of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate. The solution was vacuum dried and reconstituted by adding 2% Acetonitrile (ACN) and 0.1% Formic acid (FA) to an equal peptide concentration. The separation process was conducted using a nano-liquid chromatography system. Initially, an enrichment and desalting step was executed using a trap column where the sample underwent separation in a tandem self-packed C18 column (150 μm inner diameter, 1.8 μm particle size, 32 cm length), employing an effective gradient flow rate of 500 nL/min: 0-5 min, 5% mobile phase B (98% ACN, 0.1% FA); 5-45 min, mobile phase B linearly increased from 5% to 25%; 45-50 min, mobile phase B increased from 25% to 35%; 50-52 min, mobile phase B increased from 35% to 80%; 52-54 min, 80% mobile phase B; 54.5-65 min, 5% mobile phase B. 
Eluting peptides were ionized via a CSI nano-source and subsequently introduced into the tandem mass spectrometer, TimsTOF Pro (Bruker Corporation, Billerica, MA), for detection in Data-Dependent Acquisition (DIA) mode. The principal parameter settings were set as follows: the voltage of the ion source was set at 1.6 kV; the range of ion mobility was 0.75 - 1.40 V·s/cm², and the scan range of the primary mass spectrometry was between 100 - 1700 m/z. The range of 395 - 1195 m/z was divided into 4 steps, and each step was further subdivided into 8 windows, amounting to 32 windows for continuous window fragmentation and information acquisition. The fragmentation mode was CID, with a fragmentation energy of 10 eV. The mass width of each window was 25 Da, with the cycle time for each DIA scan set at 0.95 s.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files from the spectral library were processed utilizing DIA-NN (version 1.9.2) in library-free mode, adhering to the default settings specified under "robust LC (high precision)." The precursor ions were analyzed within an m/z range of 300 to 1800 and a charge state range of 1 to 4. Protein identification was achieved through in-silico tryptic digestion at 1% FDR, employing the UniProt database for reference (UP000005640, 82,685 proteins, Aug 2024). The Mass Spectrometry Downstream Analysis Pipeline (MS-DAP) (Version 1.2.1) was used for quality control.
